I'm identifying the 3x3 prototype shape and other scattered shapes, then figuring out the rule: each of the 8 directions from the origin gets scaled by a step of 4 based on the direction's components.

For each direction, I check the color present at the first step offset and use that to color a chain of copies extending in that direction—right gives color 2, down gives color 3, up-right gives color 4, and so on—while directions with no color present at that offset default to background.

Up-right color4 copies follow the same pattern at rows3-5 cols10-12, then wrap to rows -1..1 cols14-16, with out-of-bound rows clipped naturally. I check the iteration bound k=1..7 confirms further copies fall outside the grid, and note that overlapping marker cells at those positions get overwritten by the shape copies.

Now I'm laying out the full 21x21 grid row by row: placing the color4 pattern near rows0-5, then the 8/2 shapes across rows7-9 at columns 6-8, 10-12, 14-16, 18-20, followed by the 3-pattern shapes repeating at rows11-13 and 15-17.

For the offset logic: each of 8 directions gets a "crement" transformation applied to the (h,w) product, then copies are placed at multiples of that offset out to the grid edge, with the color determined by whichever non-background color appears at the first copy's location—matching how the example correctly assigned colors 1, 7, and 5 to different directions. Now I'm applying this same directional logic to the current puzzle's 3x3 prototype, checking each of the eight offset directions to see which color occupies the shifted cell block, starting with the "up" direction which lands on the 5-colored cells.

I'm confirming that the diagonal "up-right" offset lands on cells colored 9, while other directions land purely on background cells, meaning those directions won't produce visible copies since coloring with background leaves the grid unchanged. So only two directions—up and up-right—actually produce visible copies, using colors 5 and 9 respectively, and now I'm working out the specific offset positions for each successive copy along the "up" direction.

For the up-right direction, k=1 gives cells at rows4-6 cols13-15 forming the 9-shape, and k=2 gives the same shape shifted to rows0-2 cols17-19, both colored 9. The original 9-shape cells overlap with the k=1 copy, so they get overwritten anyway.
